name: Faturatik E-Arşiv Fatura Entegrasyonu
author: faturatik

sections.description:
Faturatik E-Arşiv Invoice Integration connects your WooCommerce store with the Faturatik e-invoice platform. Your orders are automatically sent to Faturatik and e-archive invoices are generated.

Features

  • Automatic Order Submission – Orders are automatically sent to Faturatik at the status you specify
  • Manual Submission – Create invoices with one click from order details
  • Bulk Submission – Send multiple orders at once
  • Invoice Status Tracking – View invoice status in order list and details
  • Customer Invoice Fields – Tax ID and tax office fields at checkout
  • My Account Page – Customers can track their invoices
  • Webhook Integration – Receive invoice status changes instantly
  • Automatic Retry – Failed submissions are automatically retried
  • WooCommerce HPOS Compatible – High-Performance Order Storage support

Requirements

  • WordPress 6.0 or higher
  • WooCommerce 8.0 or higher
  • PHP 8.0 or higher
  • An active Faturatik account

Setup

  1. Install and activate the plugin
  2. Go to WooCommerce > Settings > Faturatik tab
  3. Enter the API token from Faturatik Panel
  4. Test the connection
  5. Configure automatic submission settings
sections.installation:
1. Upload the faturatik-woocommerce folder to /wp-content/plugins/
  2. Activate the plugin through the WordPress admin panel
  3. Configure via WooCommerce > Settings > Faturatik
sections.faq:
Where can I get the API token?

You can create an API token at Faturatik Panel.

What invoice types are supported?

E-Invoice and E-Archive Invoice are supported. The invoice type is automatically determined based on your settings in Faturatik Panel.

How does the webhook work?

You need to add the Webhook URL and Secret shown in the plugin settings to your store settings in Faturatik Panel. This way, invoice status changes are instantly reflected on your site.

What happens if orders fail to send?

Failed submissions are automatically retried. A maximum of 3 attempts are made (at 5 minute, 30 minute, and 1 hour intervals).
